titleText.es: La buena noticia es que, según el último informe del IPCC, si aprobamos límites agresivos para las emisiones ahora mismo, podemos limitar el calentamiento a 2°. Eso es solo MEDIA unidad de edad de hielo, lo cual no es para tanto.
titleText.en: The good news is that according to the latest IPCC report, if we enact aggressive emissions limits now, we could hold the warming to 2°C. That's only HALF an ice age unit, which is probably no big deal.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and official English title attributes are preserved exactly. The source uses a deliberately invented UEH scale; all temperatures, scale positions, years, depths, and sea-level magnitudes are audited as excluded measurements or numbers. OCR lost several accents, fused EN LOS and DE HIELO, split ÚLTIMA and ESTADO, and omitted the large zero and question mark.

Rápidamente is formed from rápida plus -mente and describes how the limits would be set.

Agresivos takes masculine plural form to agree with límites.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.

example.en: If you have time, call.

cards.noteEn: Ponemos is the present form of poner for nosotros. With límites it means setting or imposing limits.

example.en: We set clear limits on the project.

cards.questionEn: How do you turn many describing words into words such as “quickly,” “clearly,” or “probably”?
cards.answerEn: Use the feminine singular form of the describing word and add -mente. If its masculine and feminine forms are identical, simply add -mente.
cards.noteEn: For an adjective that changes, use its -a form: claro becomes clara and then claramente. For one form shared by both genders, probable becomes probablemente. The new word usually describes how an action happens or how the speaker judges a claim.

example.en: Lucía answers clearly.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

example.en: I need a new backpack.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: For a policy or limit, agresivo can mean forceful or stringent rather than physically violent.

example.en: The plan includes aggressive targets.

cards.answerEn: on; to (introducing what a limit applies to)
cards.noteEn: A can introduce the activity or quantity constrained by a limit.

example.es: El país puso límites a las emisiones.
example.en: The country put limits on emissions.

cards.answerEn: a made-up ice-age unit that makes projected warming visually comparable with major past climate change
cards.noteEn: The chart defines one unit as the roughly 4.5-degree global difference between the coldest part of the last ice age and a modern reference. It then places projected warming on that scale. This exposes how a few degrees of global average warming can represent a climate shift comparable in magnitude to moving out of an ice age, with radically different coastlines and polar conditions.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a finales de, “in the late part of”
cards.noteEn: The preposition a is required in the time expression a finales de. Natural English normally renders the full expression with “in,” not by translating a alone.

example.en: They arrived in late June.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something happens in the late part of a month, year, decade, or other period?
cards.answerEn: Use a finales de, followed by the period.
cards.noteEn: A is fixed in this expression, finales is the plural of final, “end,” and de introduces the period. English commonly says “in late…” or “at the end of…,” depending on context.

example.es: El curso termina a finales de julio.
example.en: The course ends in late July.

cards.answerEn: late part; end (in a finales de)
cards.noteEn: Final means “end.” Its plural form finales is used in a finales de to locate something near the end of a month, year, decade, or other period.

example.es: La tienda abrió a finales de verano.
example.en: The store opened in late summer.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces the period after a finales de
cards.noteEn: In a finales de, de connects the expression to the period whose late part is meant. English normally folds the whole expression into “in late…” rather than translating de separately.

example.en: We will return in late May.

cards.noteEn: This sense names the planet rather than land or soil.

example.es: La Tierra gira alrededor del Sol.
example.en: Earth revolves around the Sun.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; presents the thing as changing
cards.noteEn: With verbs such as reducir and ampliar, se lets Spanish describe a change without naming anyone who causes it. English often uses a simple verb such as “shrinks” or “widens.”

example.en: The stain shrinks.

cards.answerEn: will have (helper for a completed future action)
cards.noteEn: Habrá is the future form of the helper haber for one person or thing. Before a completed-action form such as terminado, it helps build “will have finished.”

example.en: Marta will have finished tomorrow.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that an action will already be complete by a future point?
cards.answerEn: Use a future form of haber, then the action's completed-action form.
cards.noteEn: The helper changes with the person: habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán. The following completed-action form stays unchanged: habrá llegado means “will have arrived.”

example.en: By Friday, we will have finished.

cards.noteEn: Calentado is the completed-action form of calentar used after haber.

example.es: El sol habrá calentado el agua.
example.en: The sun will have warmed the water.

cards.noteEn: De is fixed with media in the statistical expression de media. Its meaning comes from the complete expression rather than the usual possession or origin senses.

example.en: Ten messages arrive on average.

cards.questionEn: How do you state that a number is an average?
cards.answerEn: Use de media after the measured quantity or statement.
cards.noteEn: De media is a compact statistical expression meaning ‘on average.’

example.es: La clase dura cincuenta minutos de media.
example.en: The class lasts fifty minutes on average.

cards.noteEn: Media is the feminine noun for an average. In de media it describes a typical value across many cases.

example.es: La media es de ocho horas.
example.en: The average is eight hours.

cards.promptEs: entre + elemento A + y + elemento B
cards.questionEn: How do you frame two endpoints or sides as a range, pair, or contrast?
cards.answerEn: Place entre before the first endpoint or side and y before the second one.
cards.noteEn: Entre marks the range or pair involved, and y joins its two sides. Each side may be a single word or a longer noun group.

example.es: No veo la diferencia entre el azul oscuro y el negro.
example.en: I do not see the difference between dark blue and black.

cards.answerEn: Write qué, cómo, cuándo, and similar words with an accent when they ask a question or add an exclamation.
cards.noteEn: This includes direct questions (¿Qué quieres?), questions inside another sentence (No sé qué quiere), and exclamations (¡Qué bonito!). Without the accent, these words usually connect parts of a sentence instead: el libro que quiero means “the book that I want.”
cards.questionEn: Why do words such as que, como, and cuando sometimes have a written accent?

example.en: What is your name?

cards.noteEn: Before a specific moment, en can correspond to English “at.”

example.en: He arrived at just the right moment.

cards.questionEn: How do you describe someone or something as the most of a quality?
cards.answerEn: Use the matching form of “the,” name the person or thing, then add más plus the describing word.
cards.noteEn: The opening el, la, los, or las agrees with the noun. Más stays unchanged, while the final adjective changes when Spanish normally requires agreement.

example.en: It is the longest street.

cards.noteEn: Más normally means “more.” After el, la, los, or las, it can instead mark the highest degree in a group: la más rápida means “the fastest one.”

example.en: Ana is the fastest.

cards.noteEn: Frío is the masculine singular temperature adjective. After más with a definite comparison it can mean ‘coldest.’

example.es: Enero fue el mes más frío.
example.en: January was the coldest month.

cards.answerEn: in; among (introducing what ‘best’ or ‘worst’ is compared across)
cards.noteEn: After a highest-or-lowest description such as el mejor or el peor, de can introduce the full group or time range being compared.

example.es: Es la mejor canción de la década.
example.en: It is the best song of the decade.

cards.promptEs: número ordinal antes de un sustantivo
cards.questionEn: How do you use words such as first, second, or third before a Spanish noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the ordinal before the noun and make its ending match the noun's gender and number.
cards.noteEn: An ordinal gives a position in an order. Primero, segundo, tercero, último, and similar words usually come before the noun. Most forms use -o with a masculine singular noun and -a with a feminine singular noun, but primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun. Plural nouns use plural forms.

example.es: La segunda puerta está en el tercer piso.
example.en: The second door is on the third floor.

cards.noteEn: Era is a past form of ser used for a background state, description, or ongoing past situation. This form is called the imperfect.

example.en: The house was small.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that one thing is more of a certain quality than another?
cards.answerEn: Put más before the describing word and que before the other thing.
cards.noteEn: The describing word is an adjective, such as alto for “tall” or importante for “important.” Más raises the degree, and que introduces what you compare it with.

example.es: Este libro es más corto que aquel.
example.en: This book is shorter than that one.

cards.noteEn: Fría describes one feminine person or thing and carries a written accent on í.

example.en: The water is cold.

cards.noteEn: Here norma means the reference level treated as normal, not a rule that tells people what to do.

example.es: La temperatura está por debajo de la norma.
example.en: The temperature is below the norm.

cards.noteEn: Del is the required contraction of de + el. It can mean “of the” or “from the,” depending on context.

example.en: I’m coming from the market.

cards.noteEn: Llamemos is the nosotros command form of llamar used to propose a shared name or label.

example.es: Llamemos unidad solar a esta cantidad.
example.en: Let's call this quantity a solar unit.

cards.promptEs: propuesta para nosotros: hablemos, comamos, vivamos
cards.questionEn: How do you propose an action for a group that includes yourself, like “let's talk”?
cards.answerEn: Use the special “we” proposal form: most -ar verbs take -emos, while most -er and -ir verbs take -amos.
cards.noteEn: Start from the verb's dictionary form, the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Hablar becomes hablemos, comer becomes comamos, and vivir becomes vivamos. Some verbs also change their spelling or base, so learn unfamiliar forms as you meet them.

example.en: Let's look for another table.

cards.questionEn: How do you assign a proposed name to a person or thing?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of llamar, state the name, and introduce the thing receiving it with a.
cards.noteEn: The name comes directly after llamar. The a-phrase identifies what receives that label; in English the same relation is often expressed with ‘call’ and no separate equivalent of a.

example.es: Llamamos zona segura a este espacio.
example.en: We call this space a safe zone.

cards.noteEn: A unidad can be an agreed amount used to measure and compare other amounts.

example.es: El metro es una unidad de longitud.
example.en: The metre is a unit of length.

cards.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’

example.en: I need a coffee cup.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces what receives a name
cards.noteEn: With llamar, a can introduce the person or thing that is assigned the stated name.

example.en: We call that direction north.

cards.noteEn: This is a condition or situation, not a political state.

example.es: Comprobamos el estado actual del sistema.
example.en: We check the current state of the system.

cards.noteEn: Spanish actual means current, not usually English ‘actual.’

example.en: The current state is stable.

cards.noteEn: Before a length of time, hace tells you how long ago something happened. It does not mean “does” in this use.

example.en: I arrived two hours ago.

cards.questionEn: How do you say how long ago a past event happened?
cards.answerEn: Put hace before the length of time.
cards.noteEn: Spanish places hace before a duration: hace dos semanas means “two weeks ago.” The verb that describes the event itself is normally in a past form.

example.en: We met three months ago.

cards.noteEn: Años is the plural of año. Keep the ñ: anos without it is a different word.

example.en: We lived there for two years.

cards.noteEn: Actualidad refers to what is current now. It does not mean the English word ‘actuality.’

example.es: El gráfico llega hasta la actualidad.
example.en: The graph reaches the present day.

cards.noteEn: Dentro de followed by a length of time looks forward from now: dentro de una semana means “in a week.”

example.en: I will return in an hour.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something will happen a certain amount of time from now?
cards.answerEn: Use dentro de before the length of time.
cards.noteEn: Dentro de looks forward from the present: dentro de dos horas means “in two hours.” This differs from hace dos horas, which looks backward and means “two hours ago.”

example.es: El tren sale dentro de media hora.
example.en: The train leaves in half an hour.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes dentro de, “in”
cards.noteEn: When dentro de introduces a future delay, translate the two words together as “in.”

example.es: La película empieza dentro de diez minutos.
example.en: The movie starts in ten minutes.

cards.noteEn: As a noun, invernadero is a structure kept warm for plants. It can also evoke extremely warm climate conditions.

example.en: The greenhouse retains heat.

cards.noteEn: Cretácico names the geological period roughly 145 to 66 million years ago.

example.es: El clima cretácico era muy cálido.
example.en: The Cretaceous climate was very warm.

cards.noteEn: Subida can name an upward movement or an increase in a measured level.

example.es: La subida del nivel fue rápida.
example.en: The rise in the level was rapid.

cards.questionEn: How do you say ‘sea level’ in Spanish?
cards.noteEn: Del combines de and el. The expression names the reference height of the sea's surface and is common in geography and climate discussions.

example.es: La ciudad está cerca del nivel del mar.
example.en: The city is near sea level.

cards.noteEn: Here polos means the geographic North and South Poles, not rods, magnets, or clothing.

example.es: Los polos reciben poca luz en invierno.
example.en: The poles receive little light in winter.
